mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) rising above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases risk aversion, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent fall in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand drivers, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) and negative S&P 500 20-day returns exists during periods of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), reflecting labor-market weakness amplifying recession risk.
failure_condition: The correlation between UNRATE and 20-day negative S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) during FEDFUNDS > 4.0% periods.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) is above its 12-month moving average and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, a rise in INDPRO by more than 0.5% month-over-month predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to improved growth expectations.
regime_hint: expansionary labor market and above-trend industrial production
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered expansionary regime episodes.
